cities.d: (الرياض) — the capital of and the largest city in the Kingdom

x.around: Riyadh is very much a car-oriented city, although the Riyadh Metro finally provides an alternative. There are no street addresses as such in Riyadh, as mail is delivered to post office boxes, so getting around requires knowing landmarks near the place where you want to go.

hidden.d: This stadium has closed for reconstruction. It's being expanded to 92,000 capacity and will host soccer matches in the AFC Asian Cup Finals in 2027.

x.intro: Riyadh (الرياض ar-Riyāḍ) is the capital of Saudi Arabia, slightly east of the center of the country in the heart of the Tuwaig escarpment.

must.d: Undoubtedly Riyadh's most stunning piece of modern architecture, at 305 m the Kingdom Centre is the second tallest building in Saudi Arabia and quite a sight, especially when lit up at night.
The heart of old Riyadh, this was the fortress stormed by King Abdul Aziz and his men in their daring reconquest of Riyadh in 1902.
This museum (opened in 1999) is done up with the latest technology and is very accessible to visitors, with almost everything available in English.
Riyadh's second old mud-brick palace, built by King Abdul Aziz after he conquered Masmak Fortress and figured he should built something harder to conquer.
Next to the Great Mosque and the mutawwa headquarters, this nondescript expanse of cement is known by expats as Chop-Chop Square as convicts are publicly beheaded with a scimitar here.

next.d: the largest port on the Red Sea and the gateway to Mecca and Medina, but with good scuba diving too
if you have a car, the 4-hour drive through the desert to the comparatively liberal state of Bahrain is not too bad

The new luxurious party city of the Middle East. If you have a car, it will be a 10-hour drive east through the desert. For cheap flights, approximately 1½ hours, take a low-cost airline into Sharjah.
Saudi Arabian Airlines & Middle Eastern Airlines provide excellent connections multiple times a day. If you are for drinking on a plane, MEA will be your choice, as Saudia does not serve alcohol on…
This Arabian treasure provides an excellent home base for exploring Oman and its natural and cultural heritage with great opportunities for experienced and novice scuba divers alike.

x.safe: Riyadh is more conservative than Jeddah or the Eastern Province. Women mostly cover themselves with an abaya (available in shops everywhere in Riyadh) but covering the face has become less common as of 2018. People no longer expect non-Arab women to cover their hair, but showing excessive skin might draw unwanted attention, even in the areas most used to tourists.

cities.d: (أَبْهَا) — a summer tourist mountain resort city in the southwest near the Yemeni border

x.intro: Abha is a city in Saudi Arabia. The capital of Asir province, its high altitude makes it a popular summer getaway for Saudis.

next.d: well worth a visit, especially for the old Governor's Palace in mud brick.

cities.d: (الظهران) — the home of Saudi Aramco, the world's largest petroleum company
(جِدَّة) — a large metropolitan city on the Red Sea, known for its distinctive coral houses in the old town

x.around: Many rental agencies like Avis or Budget will rent you a 2008 mid-size car for the price of SR100-140 per day. You'll also find a bargain when it comes to fuel, as Saudi Arabia has some of the cheapest petrol prices in the world. The streets are wide and signs are written in both Arabic and English. Look for maps in the libraries or big supermarkets.

hidden.d: An interactive digital museum that covers a hectare. It features over 80 immersive artworks designed for physical play and all-age exploration.

At the heart of the old city, coral houses line both sides of this busy market street. A photography permit is theoretically necessary (inquire at the office behind Naseef house), but in practice nobody seems to bat an eyelid as…
This no longer has a resident soccer club. It's being expanded to 27,000 for the 2027 AFC Asian Cup Finals.
An Ottoman qishla (fort) built in the 1800s.

x.intro: Jeddah (Arabic: جدّة, also spelled Jiddah) is on the Red Sea in western Saudi Arabia. It is the kingdom's second largest city, with a population of approximately 3,400,000, and a major commercial center in the country. Jeddah is also the main entry point, either by air or sea, for pilgrims making the Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca and Medina, the two most sacred cities of Islam. Both are a few hours inland from Jeddah.

must.d: With a maximum height between 260 and 312 m, this fountain in the Red Sea is the tallest in the world. Water ejected reaches supersonic speeds of 375 km/h, and the amount of water in the air can exceed 16 m³.
The former house of one of Jeddah's main trading families is being renovated as a museum and cultural center. Great views from the top floors when it's open.

x.safe: While Jeddah is not as conservative as Riyadh, it is recommended that you follow the various safety tips in Saudi Arabia article to stay out of trouble.

cities.d: (مكة) — the holiest city in Islam and commonly visited as part of the Hajj pilgrimage; off-limits to non-Muslims

x.around: Mecca's transportation network is well developed, however, expect getting around to be a literal hassle during the Hajj; millions of pilgrims are in every nook and corner of the city, and it can take ages to get to one place from another.

hidden.d: The only place in Saudi Arabia where Kiswa is traditionally made to mark the beginning of Hajj.

n.en: The Kiswa Factory of the Holy Ka'aba

hidden.d: This museum has a lot of historical artifacts from different eras.
The museum has an impressive collection of Islamic artifacts that all tell interesting tales of Mecca and its rich culture.

x.intro: Mecca, officially known as Makkah al-Mukarramah (Arabic: مكة المكرمة, Makkah al-Mukarramah), is a major city in Saudi Arabia and the holiest city in Islam.

must.d: At the center of the grand mosque is the Kaaba, which according to Muslim traditions was built by the Prophet Abraham and his son, the Prophet Ishmael.
The holiest site in Mecca and Islam is Grand Mosque. The massive mosque is the world's largest mosque and can accommodate up to 2 million people at once.
70m (230 ft) high Hill of Arafat is a granite hill in the outskirts of Mecca is the site where Prophet Muhammad stood and delivered the Farewell Sermon to the Muslims during the last day of his life.
These were the two small hills now well transformed into long galleries which are well-constructed with marble floor and equipped with air-conditions.

The cave of Hira is an important site, since atop the mountain locally known as Jabal Al Noor is where Muslims believe Muhammed first had the Quran revealed to him from Allah through the angel Jebril.

Mina is a neighborhood of Mecca. It has the nick name of Tent City, as there are hundred of thousands of air-conditioned tents in the area, which act as temporary accommodations for pilgrims during Hajj time.
This is the cemetery in which companions and relatives of Prophet Muhammed are buried, including his first wife, uncle, grandfather, great-grandfather, and great great-grandfather.
This is the cave in which Prophet Muhammed hid in as he made departure to Yathrib (now Medina) from Mecca while being pursued by Quraish of Mecca who were planning to harm him.

next.d: Islam's second holiest city. Unlike Mecca, Medina is open to non-Muslims.
the unofficial summer capital of Saudi Arabia. Non-Muslims are allowed to enter.
the second largest city in Saudi Arabia, known for the traditional coral houses in its old town.

x.safe: The various safety tips found in the Saudi Arabia article will come in handy. Refer it to often to stay out of trouble.

cities.d: (المدينة) — the resting place of the Prophet Muhammad, and the second holiest city in Islam

hidden.d: A smaller, private museum that hosts a number of models of old Medina.
This museum uses models, holograms and video to present a minutely detailed view of the Prophet’s daily life and character.

n.ar: المعرض والمتحف الدولي للسيرة النبوية والحضارة الإسلامية
n.en: The International Fair and Museum of the Prophet's Biography and Islamic Civilization

x.intro: Medina (Arabic: المدينة, Madinah), officially known as Al-Madinah al-Munawwarah (Arabic: المدينة المنورة, al-Madīnah al-Munawwarah), is a city in the Hejaz region of Saudi Arabia.

must.d: The Masjid Nabawi, or the Prophet's Mosque, is the second most important pilgrimage site in Islam, where devout Muslims offer prayers.
This is either the oldest mosque in the world or the second-oldest, and dates from the time of the Prophet Muhammad. New construction was added in 1984.
A huge graveyard, where most family members and companions of the Prophet are buried. It is only open for a few hours each day.
Further away is the Masjid al-Qiblatayn where the Quran recounts that the Prophet was ordered by Allah to turn his face from Jerusalem to the Kaaba in Makkah while offering prayers.
Other things to be seen, a little away from the city, are the plains and mountain of Uhud where the battle took place.
Masjid Jumua where the Prophet prayed the first Jumua or Friday prayers.
Masjid Gamama where once he had prayed for rain.
One of few non-religious sites in Medina, this museum showcases the history of Medina from prehistoric to modern time.

cities.d: (نجران) — a Yemeni-influenced city with a remarkable fortress

x.intro: Najran (previously Aba as Sa'ud) is the principal city of Najran province in south-western Saudi Arabia.

next.d: border, land travel across may not be possible, and is certainly not recommended due to the high level of violence in the area.

cities.d: (اَلطَّائِفُ‎) — the unofficial summer capital of the Kingdom

x.around: If you are considering renting a car during your stay in the city, here are a few companies to choose from. As with any service, do your due diligence and research, and do check if your drivers license is valid in Saudi Arabia.

hidden.d: A triple-arched gate to the old city.
The largest rose oil factory in the city (and probably the whole of Saudi Arabia), it has been run and owned by the Al-Gadhi family for more than a hundred years.
A park situated in the Wadi Leh valley.
Hop on a cable car and feast your eyes on the fantastic scenery of Ta'if! The cable car network is said to be the largest network in Saudi Arabia and the Middle East.
An abandoned, historical palace.
An expansive theme park with multiple amenities for children.
A dam situated in the Wadi Leh valley. You can take a stroll here if you wish.
A historical building that includes a number of Islamic decorations and Roman pillars.

x.intro: Ta'if (pronounced "Taayef", also written as "Taif") is a city in the Mecca province of Saudi Arabia. With a population of 690,000 people (2020 estimate), it is the sixth most populous city in Saudi Arabia.

must.d: Was once the largest and best known open-air market in the Islamic world. Now hosts multiple events such as poetry recital competitions, arts and crafts exhibitions, and so on.

next.d: Islam's holiest city. Non-Muslims are not allowed to enter.
Islam's second holiest city. Non-Muslims are allowed to enter, but they're disallowed from entering certain areas.
the second largest city in Saudi Arabia.

x.safe: Ta'if is an extremely safe city. You're unlikely to face any major dangers. As Ta'if is a popular destination among Saudis, people go to great lengths to keep the city safe.

intro: Saudi Arabia (Arabic: السعودية, as-Suʿūdīyah) is the quintessential Arab kingdom. Vast deserts, scorching heat, immense oil wealth, camel races, glitzy shopping malls, traditional souq markets, you can find every Arabian cliche you can think of and then some here.

other.d: (Rub' al Khali) — one of the largest sand deserts on earth

x.around: A caravan of 4WD vehicles or camels are the only sane options for entering the soft sands of the desert.
x.intro: The Empty Quarter (Arabic: الربع الخالي‎, Rub'al-Khali) is the large, expansive desert encompassing a large part of the Arabian Peninsula. It's the largest continuous body of sand in the world.
x.safe: Never drive alone, even if you're an experienced driver. Much of the Empty Quarter is barren and you can get easily lost if you don't know what you're doing. For all you know, you can unexpectedly end up in a completely foreign land and you may find it difficult to get back to where you started.

other.d: (Madain Saleh) — Ruined Nabataean city similar to Petra, a

x.around: If you are staying at one of the fancy hotels, you will most likely get arranged a transport to the Winter Park Visitor Center and to all the other relevant locations in the region.

hidden.d: A bit off the beaten path, but highly recommended. A giant rock arch of about 100 m length, picturesquely located inside a rocky valley.
Contains the largest of all Hegra tombs, the Qasr al-Bint, a series of tombs carved up to 16 meters high.
Tombs cut on the eastern and western sides of four parallel rock outcrops. Façade decorations are small in size.
It is usually part of the Jabal Ikhmal Day Tour. Visitors can carve their name in ancient Nabatean language onto small rocks, which they can take home as souvenirs afterwards.

A very picturesque rock formation and scenic place to take pictures from the surrounding rocks. The actual bottom of Elephant Rock can only be accessed by paying entrance fee of a café that surrounds the whole rock.
The largest necropolis, consisting of numerous outcrops separated by sandy zones, although only eight of the outcrops have cut tombs, totaling 48 in quantity.

x.intro: Hegra (ٱلْحِجْر al-Ḥijr), also Madain Saleh (مدائن صالح) is a large archaeological site in Hejaz, Saudi Arabia.

next.d: about a 330-km car ride south-east of Al-Ula, is commonly referred to as the "cradle of Islamic culture and civilisation". It is Islam's second holiest city.
about a 360-km car ride south of Al-Ula, is famous for its Red Sea scuba diving options and petrochemical industry.

x.safe: Al-Ula/Hegra is as safe as the rest of Saudi Arabia. However, three French nationals were killed in the area in 2007, presumably by terrorists. Since then the region is considered safe though, and annually the inflow of tourists is increasing dramatically.
